guideTitle: 6 Best Bluetooth Trackers for Wallets in 2026
metaDescription: Six slim wallet tracker cards compared on thickness, ring volume, charging and phone support, so you can pick a card that fits your wallet and your phone.
introParagraphs: A wallet is the one item you cannot easily replace in an afternoon, and it is also the item that slides under a car seat or into a coat you forgot you owned. A wallet tracker is built differently from a keychain tag: it is a flat card that sits with your other cards, so thickness and charging matter more than a keyring hole.

We evaluated six cards based on product specs and buyer feedback, comparing thickness, ring volume, how long a charge lasts and which phone network each one needs. Three work with either Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, one is Apple only, one runs on Tile's own app, and one lists a very long sealed battery life.
Check the thickness and the charging method first, because a card that bulges the wallet or needs a pad you do not own gets left behind.

products.name: UQO Wallet Tracker Card, Find My or Find Hub
specs: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The UQO card is the best all-rounder because it matches a standard credit card footprint and works on either phone network. The listing gives exact numbers: 85.6 x 54 x 2.85 mm and 13.6 g, so it fits most wallets, card holders and passport sleeves. It pairs through Apple Find My as an Other Supported Item or through the Google Find Hub prompt, with no separate UQO app or subscription.

Power is rechargeable on any compatible Qi pad. About 1 hour of charging buys roughly 2 to 3 months, and an orange or green light shows charging or full. The ringer is rated 85 dB or more, separation alerts are available, and Lost Mode and sharing are supported. The tradeoff is the frequent top up, since 2 to 3 months is shorter than some rivals.

If you already own a Qi pad the routine is painless. Compared with the Spotminders PRO at up to 8 months per charge it needs charging more often, but it works on Android too, which the Spotminders does not. Against the Ridge at 95 dB it is a little quieter.
products.bestFor: Anyone who wants a credit card sized tracker that works on iPhone or Android.
pros: Works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so either phone is covered
Credit card footprint at 2.85 mm and 13.6 g fits most wallet slots
About 1 hour on a Qi pad gives 2 to 3 months of use per the listing
Separation alerts, Lost Mode and sharing are all supported in the app
cons: Needs a charge every 2 to 3 months, more often than some rivals do
At 85 dB or more it is quieter than the Ridge's 95 dB or KIUP's 120 dB
Requires a Qi wireless pad, which is not stated as being in the box

products.name: Spotminders Wallet Tracker PRO, Apple MFi Certified
products.description:
The Spotminders PRO is the card for iPhone owners who hate charging. The listing says one wireless charge delivers up to 8 months of use, and that the card is designed to last over 5 years. It is Apple MFi certified, pairs in one tap with the Find My app, and you can ask Siri to find your wallet or play a sound. The card is described as 0.07 in thin and looks like a regular credit card.

A 100 dB speaker and left-behind alerts handle the lost-in-a-restaurant case, and the IP68 rating covers splashes and spills. The listing also mentions a Bluetooth range, but the figure is cut off, so we do not quote one. The tradeoff is platform lock, since an Android phone cannot use it, and charging needs a wireless pad.

Ownership is simple once it is in the card slot. At up to 8 months it outlasts the UQO at 2 to 3 months and the Ridge at 5 months. At 100 dB it rings louder than the UQO at 85 dB, though the KIUP lists 120 dB for Android users who need more.
products.bestFor: iPhone owners who want the longest stated time between charges and a loud ring.
pros: Listing states up to 8 months per charge, the longest rechargeable claim
Apple MFi certified with one tap pairing and Siri support for finding
A 100 dB speaker is louder than the UQO's 85 dB and the Ridge's 95 dB
IP68 protection and left-behind alerts guard against spills and taxis
cons: Apple Find My only, so Android owners cannot use this card at all
Needs a wireless charging pad, so plan for one before you buy it
The Bluetooth range figure in the listing is cut off, so it is unknown

products.name: Ridge Tracker Card, Find My and Find Hub
specs: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The Ridge card comes from a wallet maker, and it shows in how the listing describes placement. It works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so one product serves iPhone and Android owners. The ringer reaches 95 dB with up to 300 ft (90 m) of range, and the listing suggests placing the card under a cash strap or money clip for the best performance. In open areas it carries well.

A 155 mAh battery charges through any Qi or MagSafe charger and lasts up to 5 months, with no replacement needed. IP68 covers splashes and spills, proximity alerts warn you when the wallet moves out of range, and Siri can find it on iPhone. The tradeoff is placement: the note about the cash strap implies a thick stack of cards can dull the signal.

It suits minimalist wallets best. Next to the UQO at 2 to 3 months it holds a charge longer, and it rings louder than the UQO at 85 dB. The Spotminders PRO outlasts it at 8 months and rings at 100 dB, but that card works only on iPhone.
products.bestFor: Cash strap or money clip wallet users who may switch between iPhone and Android.
pros: Lists 95 dB and 300 ft (90 m) range, strong numbers for a slim card
Charges on any Qi or MagSafe pad and runs up to 5 months per charge

products.name: Chipolo CARD Rechargeable Wallet Tracker
specs: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The Chipolo CARD is the quiet, dependable choice among the wallet trackers. Its streamlined slim design suits a wallet, passport pouch or ID holder, and it works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so Android owners are covered. You ring it from the app when it is hidden nearby, or look it up on a map using the global network when it is far away.

The headline number is the battery. It charges on a Qi magnetic wireless charger and the listing says it lasts up to 1 year per charge, the longest rechargeable claim among the dual network cards here. The listing states clearly that the charger is not included, so you must supply one. Chipolo also offers a 2-year warranty with free replacement through the Amazon seller.

The listing gives no thickness, ring volume or water rating, so we avoid guessing. Compared with the UQO at 2 to 3 months per charge, the Chipolo goes far longer between top ups. Against the Spotminders PRO at 8 months it lasts longer still, though the Spotminders lists 100 dB and IP68 where the Chipolo is silent.
products.bestFor: People who want the fewest charges and the reassurance of a 2-year warranty.
pros: Lists up to 1 year per charge, the fewest top ups among dual network cards
Works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, so any phone is supported
A 2-year warranty with free replacement through the Amazon seller
Slim design suits wallets, passport pouches and ID holders alike
cons: The Qi magnetic charger is not included, so you must supply one
No thickness, ring volume or water rating is given in the listing
Only the CARD shape is offered, so it will not clip onto a keyring

products.badge: Best for Families on Any Phone
products.name: Life360 Tile Slim Wallet Tracker, iOS and Android
products.description:
The Tile Slim is Tile's thinnest tracker, meant for wallets, passports and luggage tags. It works through the free Tile app on both iPhone and Android, so a mixed household can use one app. You can ring the card from the app or track it on a map. Press the tag to ring your phone, even when the phone is silenced.

Two extras set it apart from the Find My cards: a discreet SOS alert can message your loved ones, and the card can be added to the Life360 app so things and people show on one family map. The tradeoff is that it runs on Tile's own network rather than Apple or Google, and the listing gives no thickness, battery, volume or water rating. The SOS and map features also need family on Life360.

It is the easy gift for a family with different phones. Compared with the UQO and Ridge, which use Apple or Google networks, the Tile uses its own crowd. Against the Spotminders PRO at 100 dB it offers fewer published specs but covers Android, which the Spotminders does not.
products.bestFor: Families on different phones who want one app and a discreet SOS option.

Press the card to ring your phone, even when the phone is silenced
Discreet SOS alert can notify loved ones in an unsafe situation
Can be added to Life360 so cards and family share one map view
cons: Runs on Tile's own network rather than Apple Find My or Google Find Hub
Listing gives no thickness, battery, volume or water rating figures

products.name: KIUP Wallet Tracker Card 0.06in Slim
specs: Apple Find My and Google Find Hub

specList.label: Networks
specList.value: Apple Find My or Google Find Hub

products.description:
The KIUP card is the thinnest and loudest on paper. The listing describes a 0.06 in slim card with a speaker up to 120 dB, which is louder than any rechargeable card here. It works with both Google Find Hub and Apple Find My, and the listing adds UWB distance display within Bluetooth range. It is IP68 rated against rain and splashes.

The unusual claim is the battery: the listing says 5 to 10 years of life on Android and iOS, with no charging mentioned. That removes the pad entirely, but it is a manufacturer claim we cannot verify, and a sealed card means you replace the whole tag when the cell is spent. The listing notes it is not for GPS or Huawei phones, so check your handset.

Ownership is the easiest of the group if the claim holds, since there is no pad to buy. At 120 dB it outshouts the Ridge at 95 dB and the Spotminders PRO at 100 dB. Compared with the Chipolo CARD at up to 1 year per charge, the KIUP promises far longer, but the Chipolo adds a 2-year warranty that the KIUP listing does not mention.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want no charging pad, a loud ring and a very slim card.

At 0.06 in thin it slips into a wallet slot with almost no bulk added
A claimed 5 to 10 years of battery avoids charging pads and cables
Works with Apple Find My and Google Find Hub, plus IP68 protection
cons: The 5 to 10 year battery claim is unverified and the cell is sealed

buyingCriteria.explanation: A wallet tracker that bulges your pocket gets left at home. The KIUP lists 0.06 in, the Spotminders PRO 0.07 in, and the UQO gives 2.85 mm at 13.6 g on a standard 85.6 x 54 mm card footprint. Slim wallets and card holders with a single slot are the real test. Compare thickness against your thickest existing card, and remember that a bill fold adds bulk of its own.

Most cards recharge on a Qi pad, and the gap between charges varies widely. The UQO lists 2 to 3 months, the Ridge up to 5 months, the Spotminders PRO up to 8 months and the Chipolo CARD up to 1 year. The KIUP claims 5 to 10 years sealed, with no charging at all. Pick the cycle you will remember, and confirm you own the pad, since the Chipolo lists its charger as not included.

Apple Find My works only with iPhones, and Google Find Hub works only with Android. The UQO, Ridge, Chipolo CARD and KIUP support either, chosen when you pair, while the Spotminders PRO is Apple only and the Tile uses its own network. A single card joins only one network at a time. If the household might switch phones, a dual network card keeps your options open.

A wallet is often buried under coats, and a thin card has a small speaker. The KIUP lists up to 120 dB, the Spotminders PRO 100 dB, the Ridge 95 dB and the UQO 85 dB or more. The Tile and Chipolo CARD listings give no figure. Quieter cards still work in a car or a quiet room, but a loud one helps in a noisy house.

Metal clips, thick stacks of cards and cash straps can dull a small antenna. The Ridge listing says to place the card under the cash strap or money clip for the best performance. Keep the card near the outside of a stack where possible and test the ring once after you load the wallet. A card that rings clearly on a table may sound muffled in a full wallet.

Wallets get rained on and sit in pockets with drinks. The UQO lists none, but the Spotminders PRO, Ridge and KIUP list IP68, which the listings describe as handling splashes and spills. The Chipolo CARD instead lists a 2-year warranty with free replacement through the seller. Where a card gives neither, plan on keeping it in a dry pocket.

howWeEvaluated.title: Thickness and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked how closely each card matches a real credit card. The UQO gives exact figures of 85.6 x 54 x 2.85 mm and 13.6 g, the KIUP lists 0.06 in and the Spotminders PRO 0.07 in. Cards with stated dimensions earned more trust than those with only a word like slim.

howWeEvaluated.title: Charging and battery life
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared how long a charge is claimed to last and how it is topped up. The Chipolo CARD claims up to 1 year, the Spotminders PRO up to 8 months, the Ridge up to 5 months, and the UQO 2 to 3 months from about an hour on a Qi pad. We treated the KIUP's 5 to 10 years as a claim, not a fact.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ring volume and range
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at how each card helps you find it close by. The KIUP lists up to 120 dB, the Spotminders PRO 100 dB, the Ridge 95 dB with a 300 ft range, and the UQO 85 dB or more. These are manufacturer claims, so we used them to rank cards against each other rather than as absolutes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Phone network support
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked which phones can actually use each card. The UQO, Ridge, Chipolo CARD and KIUP support Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, the Spotminders PRO is Apple only, and the Tile Slim runs on its own app. Clear, stated support counted heavily because a wrong network makes a card useless.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each card by what it does best, not by popularity. The UQO leads on balanced fit and dual network support, the Spotminders PRO on charge interval for iPhone, the Ridge on range and cash strap use, the Chipolo CARD on warranty, the Tile Slim on family tools and the KIUP on volume and thinness.

faq.q: Which wallet tracker is best for most people?
faq.a: The UQO card is the best all-round pick because it works with Apple Find My or Google Find Hub and gives exact figures of 2.85 mm and 13.6 g. iPhone owners who hate charging may prefer the Spotminders PRO at up to 8 months. Families on mixed phones can use the Life360 Tile Slim.

faq.q: Will a wallet tracker fit with all my cards?
faq.a: Usually yes, but thickness decides. The UQO lists 2.85 mm, the Spotminders PRO 0.07 in and the KIUP 0.06 in. A standard bifold with several cards adds up quickly, so measure the thickest slot and add the card thickness. Test the wallet closed before relying on it for a trip.

faq.q: Do wallet trackers need a subscription?
faq.a: The cards here that use Apple Find My or Google Find Hub, including the UQO, Ridge and Spotminders PRO, are described without a monthly plan. The Tile and Life360 apps may offer optional paid extras. Check the app before buying, because we only know what the listings state.

faq.q: Is a wallet tracker the same as GPS?
faq.a: No, and this is the most common misconception. These cards use Bluetooth to ring nearby and depend on passing phones to report their last location. If no compatible phone passes by, the position can be old. They help you recover a wallet, not stop theft.

faq.q: How often will I need to charge it?
faq.a: It depends on the model. The UQO lists 2 to 3 months from about an hour on a Qi pad, the Ridge up to 5 months, the Spotminders PRO up to 8 months and the Chipolo CARD up to 1 year. Set a reminder, and test the ring when you charge to confirm the card is healthy.

faq.q: Can metal or cash dull the signal?
faq.a: It can. The Ridge listing advises placing the card under the cash strap or money clip for best performance, which hints that thick stacks and clips may affect a slim antenna. Keep the card toward the outside of a stack where you can, and test the ring after you load the wallet.

faq.q: Can a tracker be used to follow me without my knowing?
faq.a: Certified trackers are designed so phones warn you about an unknown tracker traveling with you, which is a privacy safeguard. If you see an alert, follow the prompts on your phone. Never place a card in another person's wallet or bag without their consent.
